label: Retained readings from Second Vatican Council, Lumen gentium
summary: §16, sentence beginning Nec divina Providentia auxilia: The notice of necessary salvific helps is used in docs/hiddenness.md for the Catholic account of grace without explicit acknowledgement. It concerns help towards salvation. To settle the access objection, a further premise must connect that help with present conscious reciprocal access or a sufficient reason for its delay. §16, sentence beginning Qui enim Evangelium Christi: The qualified possibility of salvation is used in docs/hiddenness.md in the Catholic account of grace. Connecting it to the case's empirical nonresistance premise requires an actual witness and an account of the capacity and time conditions. Connecting it to openness requires a bridge from salvation to the specified conscious access.
